frontier.hypothesis: With out2's lift dead by derivation and stptr's live length invariant, the ENTIRE floor-1 residual is now confined to one atom — stptr refs 5 -> 6 on the P1 chassis — and the s17 law says the only construct that can produce it is a chain-extender whose SOURCE pseudo dies before stptr does. `base` is the obvious such source (that is the current FAKE construct); the open question is whether any OTHER block-0 pseudo holding a value one add away from base+0xFC also dies before loop1 ends, which would give a second, differently-shaped spelling to weigh against the F1 annotation.
frontier.mechanism: make_regs_eqv (cse.c:844-857) only lets the defined register stay canonical when its last use is later than the source's; every block-0 pseudo whose last use is inside block 0 therefore qualifies as a donor, and combine folds the pair back for zero bytes (combine.c:55-56 never re-adjusts reg_n_refs).
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate every pseudo live only inside block 0 in tmp/grind/func_80041188/s17/CAND/f.flow (candidates seen so far: reg 80 `base`, reg 83/84 the D_800A9A10 address arithmetic, reg 85 `saved` before its between-block use is moved) and, for each, measure the ALLOCDBG table for a stptr chain sourced from it via tmp/grind/func_80041188/s17/dump17.sh. Seconds per variant; the law predicts each outcome in advance, so any disagreement is itself a finding.

frontier.hypothesis: The honest (FAKE-free) route to distance 0 is now the better-conditioned one: s14's alt_fakefree_floor3_s14.c already satisfies requirement (A) with ordinary C (i live 99 via `i = 0x12;` first) and scores 3 at 132/132, its entire residual being a sched1 INSN_LUID emission-order cost (`li $s4,18` at slot 67 instead of 69). Both live-length sides of the residual are now closed by s16+s17, so that +2 emission-order cost is the last open quantity on the honest chassis.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c rank_for_schedule falls back to INSN_LUID on equal priority, so the slot of `li $s4,18` is decided by RTL emission order, which is decided by statement order — and s15 measured that the ONE scheduler vector that fixes it also sets reg_live_length(i) = 97 and breaks (A). Emission order and i's live length were the same variable ONLY under the statement orders tried so far.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run tools/sched_solver on alt_fakefree_floor3_s14.c asking specifically for vectors that move `li $s4,18` from slot 67 to 69 WITHOUT shortening i's live range below 99 (i.e. constrain the solver on both quantities at once rather than solving the order alone, as s15 did), then spell and measure the top vectors with s17/dump17.sh before any sandbox run.

frontier.hypothesis: Reference-count deltas on this function are QUANTIZED to +2 (the chain step is the only surviving lift; s16 killed every use-only +1 spelling), so any of s15's four two-atom inverse vectors that requires an ODD reference delta (tbl 4 -> 5, out2 3 -> 4) is unreachable in principle, not merely unspelled.
frontier.mechanism: flow.c:2081 counts a set+use chain step as +2 references; a use-only fold-back adds an insn that cse2 folds before flow ever sees it (s16 E-s16-4), so no +1 lift exists in this compiler configuration.
frontier.next_probe: Re-read s15's four inverse-solver vectors in evidence.md (E-s15-4 and the s15 vector table), classify each by the parity of every reference delta it demands, and record which survive the quantization. Any vector needing only even deltas becomes the next spelling target; the odd ones can be banked as derived kills without further measurement.
